answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be capped unless it locks a scarce stake for a long, randomly chosen period, with one stake counted only once across identities. Splitting funds among a hundred new accounts then yields no extra influence; the attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing for provable fraud. Random lock durations blunt timing games, while a nadir in activity can still leave honest newcomers a haven to join; a zephyr of cheap identities cannot cheaply manufacture weight.
